Run an allocation model on prepared data

Source: R/08-spax_run.R
spax.Rd

Experimental. spax() binds a model specification (spec_huff(), spec_clm()) to prepared data (prep_data()) and either fits the parameters that are "fit" to observed counts (obs_flows(), obs_totals()) or, when every parameter has a value, evaluates the model at those values. spax_huff() and spax_clm() do the same from raw inputs in one call.

Usage

spax(
  data,
  model,
  observed = NULL,
  starts = NULL,
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Prepared inputs: the result of prep_data().

model

A model specification: spec_huff() or spec_clm(), or an FCA specification such as spec_e2sfca().

observed

Observed counts for a model with a parameter to fit: an obs_flows() or obs_totals() object, or raw counts (see Details). NULL (the default) for a model with a value for every parameter.

starts, lower, upper

Optional starting values and bounds for the parameters being fitted, as in fit_allocation(). They are refused when nothing is fitted.

...

Fit mode: further arguments of fit_allocation() (gradient, control, lambda, tol, max_iter, norm, keep_fits, ...); output, loss and loss_args are refused. Evaluate mode: further arguments of evaluate_allocation(), for example requested_outputs.

Value

For an FCA specification on raster data, a spax object (class c("spax", "spax_result")), see spax_e2sfca(); on numeric data, a spax_access_values (class c("spax_access_values", "spax_result")), see spax_access_values-methods. For an allocation model, an object of class c("spax_allocation", "spax_result"): a list with model (the bound ae_problem), spec, observed (a list with spec, the observation as declared, target, the counts aligned to the data, and output; NULL in evaluate mode), fit (the ae_multistart_fit, in fit mode), evaluation (the ae_equilibrium, in evaluate mode), theta (the named free parameters, fitted or given; NULL when no start was selected), held (the named held values, including kappa), mode ("fit" or "evaluate") and call. See spax_allocation-methods for what to do with it.

Details

FCA indices. With raster data (prep_data() with a SpatRaster as demand) and an FCA specification (spec_2sfca(), spec_e2sfca(), spec_m2sfca(), spec_3sfca(), spec_huff2sfca()), spax() computes the index and returns the same object as the matching one-shot (spax_2sfca(), spax_e2sfca() and the others): the type, parameters and accessibility layers are identical, and call is the call of spax(). An index is computed, not fitted: observed, starts, lower, upper and ... are refused. Group lists of decay and selection and a threshold by group are matched to the demand groups of the data by name and put in their order.

FCA indices on numeric data. With numeric data (demand, supply and a travel matrix) an FCA specification gives the index at the active origins, computed by the same engine and the same rules (the cells that reach no facility are NA, and the overall layer of demand groups is the same). The result is a spax_access_values, a list with access, a matrix with one row per active origin and one column per layer, not a raster (see spax_access_values-methods). Numeric data has one supply measure, "supply", so there is one measure, and an origin with zero or unknown demand has no row. A raster sigma (a variable catchment) is refused: "a raster sigma needs raster data".

Allocation models on raster data. With raster data and an allocation model (spec_clm(), spec_huff()), spax() first converts the data to origins, on each call and without keeping anything: the cells with finite, positive demand are the origins, their IDs are the cell numbers ("843") and each has its travel to every facility; a missing or infinite travel time is an absent pair, and a cell that reaches no facility stays an origin: with spec_clm() its demand goes to the outside option, while spec_huff() has no outside option and allocates none of it. obs_totals() works as it is, and obs_flows() is keyed by cell number: counts at cells that are not origins are dropped with a message. The model then runs as on numeric data, so every step function accepts the result, and fits to the same data can be compared. See prep_data() for the conversion and its memory.

Fit mode. Some parameter is "fit". observed is needed. The counts are aligned with the data (see obs_flows()), the model is bound to the data and fit_allocation() fits it. The loss is set by the observation and the output it is compared with by its kind, so output, loss and loss_args are refused in .... Starts, bounds and optimizer settings come from the data when they are not given: starts, lower and upper are optional (see the default search in fit_allocation()). spax() always passes analytic gradients and the strict optimizer settings control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 1e3, pgtol = 1e-2), also when you give starts, unless ... gives gradient or control itself. The result does not solve the model again: it reads the selected fit. A search in which no start converged gives a warning and a result with no estimates; summary() shows the starts and as.data.frame(type = "starts") their table.

Outside counts. An observation that declares outside counts (the outside argument of obs_flows() and obs_totals()) is fitted with the outputs "flow_outside", "utilization_outside" or "utilization_outside_by_group" of fit_allocation(): the observed counts with the outside count as one more column, element or row named "(outside)", and the Poisson loss. The model needs an outside option (spec_clm() with an outside weight above 0 somewhere): with a model without one (spec_huff(), or outside = 0 everywhere) spax() stops with "outside counts need a model with an outside option (spec_clm())" before the fit. The loss arguments of the observation pass through unchanged. The printed result has a line outside that says for how many origins (or groups) the counts are used, or that the outside total is. fitted() returns the modelled counts for the full target, the "(outside)" entry included, and as.data.frame(type = "origins") adds outside_observed and outside_modelled for flows (see spax_allocation-methods).

Evaluate mode. Every parameter has a number. Nothing is fitted, so observed, starts, lower and upper are refused, and the model is evaluated once at the given values. In this version an ungrouped model with something to fit cannot hold its decay sigma; give the decay sigma = "fit", or give beta and the outside weight too to evaluate.

Observed. Besides obs_flows() and obs_totals(), observed can be a named numeric vector (facility totals) or a matrix, read as flows when the row names are origins and the column names facilities of the data, and as totals by group when the column names are the groups of the data.

What a result holds. A spax_allocation stores the bound model, the specification, the observations as aligned to the data and the fit, or the evaluation. coef() gives the free parameters (fitted or given) and the held values are in $held and in as.data.frame(x). Outputs that the fit did not compute, for instance the flows of a fit to facility totals, are computed when asked for and not stored. The step functions (predict_allocation(), check_allocation(), compare_allocations(), bootstrap_allocation()) accept the result itself: each takes the bound model and the fit (or, for prediction, the evaluation) from it. Use saveRDS() to save a result.

See also

spax_huff() and spax_clm() for one call from raw inputs.

Other allocation interface: decay_gaussian(), obs_flows(), prep_data(), spax_access_values-methods, spax_allocation-methods, spax_huff(), spec_clm()

Examples

# Mainland Cornwall: registered residents, GP FTE and travel minutes
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ])
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ])
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]
supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)

# Huff: power decay and a fitted attractiveness exponent, fitted to the flows
# of residents to their practices. Demand is the residents registered at the
# mainland practices, since the Huff model has no outside option.
d_huff <- prep_data(stats::setNames(areas$registered_in, areas$lsoa), supply, travel)
flows <- obs_flows(cornwall_flows, origin = "lsoa", facility = "practice",
                   count = "patients")
huff <- spax(d_huff, spec_huff(), observed = flows)
#> observed: 2,290 counts from 1 origin outside the data or left out by it are dropped; 5 counts at 1 facility outside the data are dropped (the Huff model has no outside option)
huff
#> <spax allocation> Huff model (no outside option)
#>   decay       power (sigma = exponent): fit
#>   attraction  (kappa * supply)^beta: kappa = 1, beta = fit
#>   outside     none
#>   data        336 origins x 54 facilities
#> 
#>   parameter  value   status
#>   sigma      2.393   fitted
#>   beta       0.4863  fitted
#>   v0         0       held
#>   kappa      1       held
#> 
#>   selected    scan2 (start 2 of 3); 3 of 3 starts converged
#>   boundary    none
#>   starts      default search, 15 of 15 grid points, loss poisson
coef(huff)
#>     sigma      beta 
#> 2.3928431 0.4862684 
head(as.data.frame(huff, type = "facilities"))
#>   facility_id    supply attractiveness utilization
#> 1      L82001 10.298887       3.108049   17683.864
#> 2      L82003  4.693333       2.120900    4503.766
#> 3      L82004  4.341333       2.042001   12293.328
#> 4      L82006  7.973333       2.744347   14070.002
#> 5      L82007  2.888800       1.675068    7105.921
#> 6      L82008  4.670400       2.115854    9347.930

# Conditional logit with a fitted outside weight, fitted to practice totals
d <- prep_data(stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa), supply, travel)
totals <- obs_totals(tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$practice, sum))
clm <- spax(d, spec_clm(decay_gaussian(), outside = "fit"), observed = totals)
#> observed: 2,279 counts at 1 facility outside the data are left out
summary(clm)

# The same conditional logit fitted to the flows, with the outside counts known:
# demand counts the registered residents, so each origin's outside count is its
# demand minus its counts at the practices of the data
known <- obs_flows(cornwall_flows, origin = "lsoa", facility = "practice",
                   count = "patients", outside = "known")
clm_known <- spax(d, spec_clm(), observed = known)
#> observed: 2,290 counts from 1 origin outside the data or left out by it are dropped; 5 counts at 1 facility outside the data are treated as the outside option
clm_known
#> <spax allocation> conditional logit with an outside option
#>   decay       gaussian (sigma = travel scale): fit
#>   attraction  (kappa * supply)^beta: kappa = 1, beta = 1
#>   outside     v0: fit
#>   data        336 origins x 54 facilities

#>   parameter  value    status

# Nothing to fit: evaluate at given values, with no observations
spax(d_huff, spec_huff(decay_power(sigma = 1.5), beta = 1))
#> <spax allocation> Huff model (no outside option)
#>   decay       power (sigma = exponent): 1.5
